Why did the greatest archer in the world drop his bow? The war was about to begin. Two armies faced each other. As the story goes, Arjuna said, Krishna, take my chariot to the middle. I want to see who I am fighting.
And there he saw them. His grandfather. His teacher. His cousins. His hands began to shake. His bow, Gandiva, slipped from his fingers. I cannot fight my own family, he said.
Wait, what did Krishna do? He didn't scold him. Right there, between two armies, he began to speak. Do your duty. Don't worry about the results. That talk became the Bhagavad Gita.
That's why the Gita was spoken on a battlefield. Because life is a battlefield, and every one of us has dropped our bow. Comment Gita if you have read even one verse.
